analysis.investment_thesis: Avanti is India's dominant shrimp feed player with a clean balance sheet and improving margins, but at P/E 31.7x on ~12–15% long-term earnings growth, the PEG of ~2.1 makes this a classic case of paying a growth price for a cyclical stalwart. Wait for a better entry or proof that FY25's 41% profit surge represents a new earnings step-change rather than cycle recovery.
key_strengths: Zero-debt fortress balance sheet — borrowings just INR 15 Cr against equity of INR 3,011 Cr; the business self-funds growth
ROCE of 24% signals genuine capital efficiency in a commodity-adjacent industry
FY25 EBITDA 738 Cr (+35% YoY) and OCF 584 Cr show the recovery cycle has legs for now
key_risks: PEG ~2.1 (P/E 31.7 ÷ 15% earnings CAGR) — Lynch's hard limit is 1.5; the stock is priced for perfection
Revenue growth is anemic — 9Y CAGR 12.6%, and FY25 revenue grew only 4.5% YoY despite a 41% profit surge; margin expansion can't sustain forever
Proven cyclicality — net profit collapsed 38% in FY22 (245 Cr vs 397 Cr in FY21); shrimp farming is weather- and disease-dependent
red_flags: Other income INR 166 Cr in FY25 represents ~30% of net profit — strip it out and operating earnings quality looks weaker
EBITDA halved from INR 708 Cr (FY18) to INR 346 Cr (FY22) in four years — this is a cyclical, not a compounder
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Avanti Feeds tells a clear Lynch-style story: India is the world's top shrimp exporter, Avanti owns ~50% of the shrimp feed market, and rising global protein demand should lift the tide. The business has earned its dominance — zero debt, 24% ROCE, and a recovering margin profile (operating margin up to 11.57% with EBITDA at INR 738 Cr in FY25). For a Lynch "niche dominator" checklist, it ticks many boxes.

The valuation is the dealbreaker. At P/E 31.7 against a 9-year revenue CAGR of just 12.6%, the PEG sits at ~2.1 — well above the 1.0 threshold I look for. FY25's 41% profit jump is impressive but is being driven by margin recovery and INR 166 Cr in other income (up from INR 79 Cr in FY23) rather than volume growth; revenue only grew 4.5% in FY25. That's a stalwart or cyclical masquerading as a fast grower. I'd rather own this at 18–20x earnings on a confirmed growth re-acceleration than chase it at 31x on what may be peak-cycle margins.
